title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.
intro: This training programme equips fund managers, distributors, service providers and supervisors with concise briefings on how investment funds are regulated in the world's leading fund domiciles and distribution markets in Europe, offshore centres and Asia Pacific.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give participants a reliable, comparable picture of fund regulation in key jurisdictions: the fund vehicles and regulator, how funds and managers are authorised, how funds are distributed and accessed cross-border, and recent developments. Participants leave able to compare jurisdictions, plan market entry and engage confidently with local regulators and advisers.
sections.What It Covers: Ireland and Luxembourg, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, France and Germany, the Cayman Islands and other offshore centres, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Singapore, Australia, Japan, and Taiwan and South Korea.
Intended Audience: Staff of fund managers, distributors and fund service providers planning or managing business in these jurisdictions
Compliance, legal, product and business development professionals responsible for fund ranges and market access
Staff of supervisory authorities and policy teams benchmarking their fund regime against other jurisdictions
Learning Objectives: Describe the fund vehicles, regulators and legal frameworks in each jurisdiction
Explain how funds and their managers are authorised, registered or licensed
Compare the routes for distributing domestic and foreign funds, including cross-border access schemes
Identify jurisdiction-specific rules that differ from international norms
Assess recent and forthcoming regulatory developments in each market
Apply the briefings to fund domicile, distribution and market entry decisions
sections.Structure and Format: Eleven country briefings designed as recorded webinars of about 30 minutes to an hour each, supported by a live Q&A session with the trainer. Each briefing follows a common structure for easy comparison, and briefings can be taken individually, as a full series or as add-ons to the global and regional briefings.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with investment funds and international fund regulation is helpful, for example from the global and regional briefings. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)

modules.title: Ireland and Luxembourg: The Leading EU Fund Domiciles
modules.summary: How the two largest EU cross-border fund centres regulate funds and managers, the vehicles they offer and the local rules that sit on top of the EU framework.
objectives: Describe the fund vehicles and regulatory structures in Ireland and Luxembourg
Explain local authorisation, governance and substance expectations for funds and management companies
Compare the two domiciles for UCITS and alternative fund launches
syllabus: Regulators and vehicles: ICAV, investment company, unit trust, FCP, SICAV and limited partnerships
Fund authorisation, fast-track and manager-supervised alternative funds, and management company rules
Cross-border distribution from both domiciles using EU passports
Recent developments: implementation of AIFMD amendments, loan-originating funds and long-term fund vehicles

modules.title: United Kingdom
modules.summary: How the UK regulates funds and managers outside the EU, its domestic fund range, and how overseas funds access UK investors and UK funds access EU investors.
objectives: Describe the UK regulatory structure, legislation and fund vehicles
Explain the FCA's authorisation and product rules for UK funds and managers
Assess cross-border access between the UK and the EU and other markets
syllabus: The FCA, FSMA and the UK fund range: UK UCITS, non-UCITS retail and qualified investor schemes
Vehicles: unit trusts, OEICs, authorised contractual schemes and long-term asset funds
The Overseas Funds Regime, national private placement and access to the EU
Recent developments: Consumer Duty, sustainability labels and reform of fund and manager rules

modules.title: Switzerland
modules.summary: How Switzerland regulates domestic funds, fund management companies and portfolio managers, and the conditions for offering foreign funds to Swiss retail and qualified investors.
objectives: Describe FINMA's role and the Swiss collective investment and financial services legislation
Explain authorisation requirements for funds, fund management companies and portfolio managers
Apply the rules for offering foreign funds to different classes of Swiss investor
syllabus: FINMA, the Collective Investment Schemes Act and the financial services and institutions acts
Vehicles: contractual funds, SICAVs, SICAFs and limited partnerships
Foreign funds: approval for retail, Swiss representative and paying agent requirements
Recent developments: the limited qualified investor fund and swing pricing practice

modules.title: France and Germany
modules.summary: How the two largest continental EU domestic fund markets regulate funds and managers, the national vehicles they use and the rules for marketing foreign funds to local investors.
objectives: Describe the regulators, legislation and fund vehicles in France and Germany
Explain national product, liquidity management and distribution rules
Identify the requirements for marketing foreign funds in each market
syllabus: France: the AMF, the Monetary and Financial Code and French retail, professional and private equity vehicles
Germany: BaFin, the Capital Investment Code, contractual funds and institutional special funds
Distribution through banks, insurers and advisers, and marketing of foreign funds
Recent developments: liquidity management tools and national fund modernisation reforms

modules.title: Cayman Islands and Offshore Centres
modules.summary: How the leading offshore fund domicile regulates hedge, private equity and other alternative funds, and how offshore funds are distributed into onshore markets.
objectives: Describe the Cayman Islands fund vehicles and the role of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority
Explain the registration regimes for open-ended and closed-ended funds
Assess governance, AML and substance expectations for offshore funds and their onshore distribution
syllabus: Vehicles: exempted companies, segregated portfolio companies, unit trusts and exempted limited partnerships
Registration of mutual funds and private funds, audit, valuation and custody requirements
Distribution into onshore markets through private placement regimes
Recent developments: AML, beneficial ownership and economic substance, and other offshore centres

modules.title: Hong Kong
modules.summary: How Hong Kong regulates funds and asset managers, the domestic vehicles it offers and its role as a gateway between Mainland China and international markets.
objectives: Describe the SFC's role, the Securities and Futures Ordinance and the fund codes
Explain authorisation of retail funds and licensing of asset managers
Assess the routes for distributing offshore funds and for Mainland cross-border access
syllabus: The SFC, licensing of asset managers and the fund manager code of conduct
Vehicles: unit trusts, open-ended fund companies and limited partnership funds
SFC authorisation of offshore funds and mutual recognition of funds
Recent developments: Mainland connect schemes, tokenised funds and virtual asset products

modules.title: Mainland China
modules.summary: How Mainland China regulates public and private funds and their managers, the progressive opening of its asset management sector to foreign firms, and the channels for cross-border investment.
objectives: Describe the roles of the CSRC, AMAC and other financial regulators
Explain licensing of public fund managers and registration of private fund managers
Identify the inbound, outbound and mutual recognition channels for cross-border investment
syllabus: The CSRC, the Securities Investment Fund Law and AMAC self-regulation
Public fund management companies, private fund managers and the bank wealth management sector
Foreign ownership, qualified investor schemes, connect schemes and mutual recognition
Recent developments: asset management rules, private fund regulation and fee reform

modules.title: Singapore
modules.summary: How Singapore regulates funds and fund managers, the domestic vehicles it offers and the routes for offering domestic and foreign funds to Singapore investors.
objectives: Describe MAS's role, the Securities and Futures Act and the Code on Collective Investment Schemes
Explain licensing of fund management companies and authorisation of retail funds
Compare the authorised, recognised and restricted scheme routes for fund offers
syllabus: MAS, the Securities and Futures Act and fund management licensing
Vehicles: unit trusts, companies, limited partnerships and the variable capital company
Authorised, recognised and restricted schemes and the ASEAN CIS Framework
Recent developments: asset tokenisation initiatives and fund centre incentives

modules.title: Australia
modules.summary: How Australia regulates managed funds and their responsible entities, the corporate collective investment vehicle, and the distribution rules shaped by superannuation and advice reforms.
objectives: Describe ASIC's role, the Corporations Act and Australian fund vehicles
Explain licensing of managers and registration of managed investment schemes
Apply design, distribution and disclosure obligations to fund offers
syllabus: ASIC, financial services licensing and the role of superannuation investors
Vehicles: registered managed investment schemes and corporate collective investment vehicles
Disclosure, design and distribution obligations and foreign manager access
Recent developments: the Asia Region Funds Passport, conflicted remuneration and private markets scrutiny

modules.title: Japan
modules.summary: How Japan regulates investment trusts and their managers, the role of its self-regulatory organisations and the policy push to grow household investment and attract new asset managers.
objectives: Describe the roles of the Japanese Financial Services Agency, SESC and self-regulatory organisations
Explain registration of investment management businesses and of domestic and foreign funds
Assess the distribution environment for domestic and foreign investment trusts
syllabus: The Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and the Act on Investment Trusts and Investment Corporations
Vehicles: contractual investment trusts and investment corporations
Notification and distribution of foreign funds and the Asia Region Funds Passport
Recent developments: expanded tax-advantaged savings accounts and customer-oriented business conduct

modules.title: Taiwan and South Korea
modules.summary: How two major North Asian distribution markets regulate domestic funds, their managers and the offering of offshore funds, including local agent and presence requirements.
objectives: Describe the regulators, legislation and fund vehicles in Taiwan and South Korea
Explain the requirements for registering offshore funds and appointing local agents
Compare public and private fund regimes and recent reforms in both markets
syllabus: Taiwan: the Financial Supervisory Commission, securities investment trust enterprises and domestic funds
Taiwan: offshore fund approval, master agents and local presence incentives
South Korea: the FSC and FSS, the Capital Markets Act, investment trusts and foreign fund registration
Recent developments: Korean private fund reform and regional asset management hub ambitions

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.

related.title: Investment Funds Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment funds and their managers, from authorisation and valuation to liquidity, leverage, private markets and tokenised funds.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.
